## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

The new flag should honor `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` so CI can configure file exclusions through the environment.

## Changes

The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag that skips files whose basenames match any supplied pattern. It logs skipped paths at info level, documents the flag, and adds tests for parsing, file collection, and archive contents.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and no `--exclude` argument, `default=[]` leaves matching files in the archive. `.agents/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` requires that “Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable”. — CI jobs that set exclusions through the environment still archive the files they intended to skip.

## Suggestions

- tests/test_main.py:20 — tests — Verify repeated exclusions in the resulting archive — With `--exclude '*.log' --exclude '*.tmp'`, this test would pass if `main()` forwarded only the first glob. It checks the parsed list, and the archive test supplies one glob. — The suite would miss a regression that silently includes files matching the second exclusion pattern. — Fix: Extend `test_main_leaves_excluded_files_out_of_the_archive` to exercise two patterns.
